title: Circular Motion — 40 MCQs
description: Covers angular displacement, velocity and acceleration, relations between angular and linear quantities, centripetal force and acceleration, motion in a vertical circle, motion of vehicles on banked surfaces, conical pendulum, and related numerical and conceptual problems.

questions.q: Angular displacement is measured in
questions.explanation: In SI the natural unit of angular displacement is the radian, defined as arc length divided by radius.

questions.q: Angular velocity ω is defined as
options: rate of change of linear displacement
rate of change of angular displacement
product of linear velocity and radius
questions.explanation: ω = dθ/dt, the time rate of change of angular displacement.

questions.q: The SI unit of angular acceleration is
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration α = dω/dt has the unit radian per second squared.

questions.q: The relation between linear speed v and angular speed ω for circular motion of radius r is
questions.explanation: Arc length s = r θ, differentiating with respect to time gives v = r ω.

questions.q: Centripetal acceleration has magnitude
questions.explanation: a_c = v² / r = r ω², directed toward the centre of the circle.

questions.q: Centripetal force is the force that
options: is required to keep a body moving in a circular path
is equal to the weight of the body
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is the net force directed toward the centre that produces the centripetal acceleration needed for circular motion.

questions.q: The direction of centripetal acceleration is
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration always points toward the centre of the circular path.

questions.q: A body moving in a circle with constant speed has
questions.explanation: Speed is constant but direction of velocity changes continuously, so acceleration (centripetal) is non-zero.

questions.q: Angular acceleration α is related to tangential linear acceleration a_t by
questions.explanation: Differentiating v = r ω with respect to time yields a_t = r α when r is constant.

questions.q: One complete revolution corresponds to an angular displacement of
questions.explanation: A full circle is 360° which equals 2π radians.

questions.q: The period T of uniform circular motion is related to angular speed ω by
questions.explanation: ω = 2π / T, therefore T = 2π / ω.

questions.q: In a conical pendulum the bob moves in a
questions.explanation: The string sweeps out a cone and the bob describes a horizontal circle at constant height.

questions.q: For a vehicle to move safely on a level circular road the necessary centripetal force is provided by
questions.explanation: On a level road the only horizontal force available is static friction, which supplies the required centripetal force.

questions.q: The frequency of revolution f is related to angular speed by
questions.explanation: One revolution is 2π rad, so ω = 2π f.

questions.q: A particle moving in a circle of radius 2 m with angular speed 3 rad s⁻¹ has linear speed
questions.explanation: v = r ω = 2 × 3 = 6 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A car of mass 1000 kg moves around a level circular track of radius 50 m at 10 m s⁻¹. The centripetal force required is
The centripetal acceleration of a particle moving with speed 4 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m is
questions.explanation: a_c = v² / r = 16 / 2 = 8 m s⁻².

questions.q: A stone tied to a string of length 0.5 m is whirled in a horizontal circle with angular speed 4 rad s⁻¹. The linear speed of the stone is
For a banked road of angle θ and radius r, the optimum speed (no friction needed) is given by
questions.explanation: Resolving forces perpendicular and parallel to the incline yields tan θ = v² / (r g), so v = √(r g tan θ).

questions.q: A particle of mass 0.2 kg moves in a vertical circle of radius 1 m. The minimum speed at the highest point so that the string remains taut is (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: At the top the critical condition is m v² / r = m g, so v = √(r g) = √10 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: The period of a conical pendulum of string length L and semi-vertical angle θ is
questions.explanation: The height of the cone h = L cos θ and T = 2π √(h / g) = 2π √(L cos θ / g).

questions.q: A body is moving in a vertical circle. The difference between the tensions at the bottom and at the top is
questions.explanation: T_bottom − m g = m v_b² / r and T_top + m g = m v_t² / r. Using energy, v_b² − v_t² = 4 g r, so T_b − T_t = 6 m g.

questions.q: A vehicle negotiates a banked curve of radius 100 m and banking angle 30°. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the safe speed (no friction) is approximately
If angular velocity is doubled for the same radius, the centripetal force becomes
questions.explanation: F_c = m r ω²; doubling ω multiplies F_c by four.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and moves with constant angular acceleration 2 rad s⁻² in a circle of radius 1 m. Its linear speed after 3 s is
questions.explanation: ω = α t = 2 × 3 = 6 rad s⁻¹; v = r ω = 1 × 6 = 6 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: The angular displacement of a rotating body in 4 s is 20 rad. Its average angular velocity is
questions.explanation: ω_avg = Δθ / Δt = 20 / 4 = 5 rad s⁻¹.

questions.q: For motion in a vertical circle the minimum speed at the bottom so that the body just completes the circle is
questions.explanation: At the top v_min = √(g r); by energy conservation v_bottom² = v_top² + 4 g r = 5 g r, so v_bottom = √(5 g r).

questions.q: A conical pendulum has a string of length 1.0 m making an angle of 60° with the vertical. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², its period is approximately
The ratio of angular speeds of the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock is
questions.explanation: Minute hand completes one revolution in 1 h; hour hand in 12 h. Therefore ω_hour / ω_minute = 1/12.

questions.q: A particle moves in a circle of radius 4 m with constant speed 8 m s⁻¹. The magnitude of its acceleration is
questions.explanation: a_c = v² / r = 64 / 4 = 16 m s⁻² (purely centripetal).

questions.q: A motorcyclist rides in a vertical loop of radius 5 m. The minimum speed at the top so that he does not fall is (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: At the top N + m g = m v² / r; for minimum speed N → 0, so v = √(r g) = √50 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A car is travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ on a banked curve of radius 100 m. The angle of banking required for no lateral friction is (g = 10 m s⁻²)
A stone of mass 0.5 kg is tied to a string of length 1 m and whirled in a vertical circle. If the speed at the lowest point is 6 m s⁻¹, the tension at the lowest point is (g = 10 m s⁻²)
The angular acceleration of a wheel increases from 2 rad s⁻¹ to 10 rad s⁻¹ in 4 s. The angular displacement during this interval is
A particle of mass m moves in a horizontal circle of radius r with constant speed v on the inside of a smooth hemispherical bowl. The normal reaction of the bowl on the particle is
questions.explanation: On a smooth surface the only radial force is the normal reaction, which supplies the centripetal force: N = m v² / r.

questions.q: A conical pendulum of length 1.2 m makes an angle of 30° with the vertical. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the linear speed of the bob is approximately
Two particles of equal mass m move in concentric circles of radii r and 2r with the same angular speed ω. The ratio of their centripetal forces is
questions.explanation: F_c = m r ω². For the same m and ω, F₁ / F₂ = r / (2r) = 1/2.

questions.q: A body slides down a frictionless track that ends in a vertical loop of radius R. The minimum height from which the body must be released to complete the loop is
questions.explanation: At the top of the loop v² ≥ g R. Energy conservation from height h: m g h = m g (2R) + ½ m (g R) ⇒ h = 2.5 R.

questions.q: A particle moves with constant angular velocity 3 rad s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m. The magnitude of its linear acceleration is
questions.explanation: Speed is constant so only centripetal acceleration exists: a = r ω² = 2 × 9 = 18 m s⁻².
